stories.headline: US and Iran pause military strikes for diplomacy amid regional drone attacks
stories.body:
The United States and Iran have paused military strikes as international mediators try to encourage diplomatic talks [c1, c11]. Following the pause in military actions, the price of international benchmark Brent crude oil dropped by more than eight per cent to US$88.36 per barrel on July 27 [c1].

Tensions had escalated earlier in July 2026 when hostilities resumed after Iranian forces attacked commercial ships in Omani waters inside the Strait of Hormuz [c2]. Advisors to US President Donald Trump had informed him that Iran was actively preparing to attack the United States unless Washington carried out a pre-emptive strike [c5]. This came after joint military strikes against Iran were launched by the United States and Israel on February 28, 2026 [c9]. Previously, in June 2026, Iran and the United States had signed a memorandum of understanding to halt military operations and reopen the Strait of Hormuz [c10].

Diplomatic efforts are currently underway to manage the crisis. Mediators led by Qatar and Pakistan are working to facilitate communications between Washington and Tehran [c11]. Speaking aboard Air Force One, US President Donald Trump stated that "there are very friendly negotiations going on" concerning the conflict [c7]. Trump also claimed that Iran had requested a meeting directly and through surrogates after it faced military strikes [c6]. However, officials in Tehran denied engaging in any direct negotiations with the United States regarding the conflict [c8].

While discussing the situation, President Trump stated that US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth "has done a great job" amid questions about military advice on Iran [c4]. But in an interview with Axios, Trump warned that the United States would resume "very strong military action" against Iran if diplomacy fails [c14].

Despite the pause in direct strikes between Washington and Tehran, conflict continues across the region. Iran-backed armed groups launched drone attacks against targets in Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Iraq following the US-Iran strike pause [c12]. Yemen's Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for targeting Saudi petroleum infrastructure, including the East-West Pipeline [c15]. At the same time, US Central Command redirected 17 commercial vessels, disabled two, and boarded two in the Strait of Hormuz to enforce a naval blockade [c13].

In unrelated economic news, the share price of Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT rose 500 per cent on its debut in Shanghai after raising US$9.8 billion in its initial public offering [c3].

people or representatives acting on behalf of someone else
stopping goods or ships from entering or leaving an area

stories.headline: Devastating wildfires in France and Spain force mass evacuations
stories.body:
Massive wildfires across southern Europe have forced hundreds of thousands of people to flee their homes [c17]. In France, fires have forced the evacuation of 220,000 people [c17]. French President Emmanuel Macron described the situation as "completely unprecedented" and called it the country's "toughest since World War Two" [c16]. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu reported that 116,085 hectares have burned and 162 arrests related to fire starts have been made since July 6 [c18]. In Cestas, Mayor Jerome Steffe said 17,000 residents were evacuated overnight after a wildfire burned 42,000 hectares and destroyed 240 houses [c19]. The National Firefighters Federation of France reported that a huge fire in southwest France created a pyrocumulonimbus fire cloud, a phenomenon never before seen in the country [c23].

In Spain, wildfires have forced more than 100,000 people to evacuate [c17]. A fire in Ávila, west of Madrid, burned 50,000 hectares, making it the largest wildfire in Spain's history [c20]. Spain's government reported that 172,000 hectares of forested land have burned this year, six times the area burned in 2025 [c21]. Meanwhile, in Italy, more than 400 people were evacuated by sea from the Gargano peninsula as a wildfire encroached on beaches in Puglia [c22].

stories.headline: New UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham hosts Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy
stories.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met new UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham in Portsmouth [c25]. Zelenskyy was Burnham's first international guest since the prime minister took office [c25]. During the visit, Burnham announced that the United Kingdom will share the intellectual property for its "Stone Cloak" electronic warfare system with Ukraine [c26]. These Stone Cloak jammers are tablet-sized devices built to stop drones from being detected [c27].

Overall, the UK has committed £25 billion in funding for Ukraine's military effort since Russia launched its full-scale invasion four years ago [c28]. Prior to leaving office, former UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer had announced £255 million in fresh funding for Ukraine during his final visit to Kyiv [c29].

The meeting took place following political changes in London. Ed Miliband now serves as Foreign Secretary in Prime Minister Burnham's government [c30]. In addition, Bridget Phillipson was appointed chair of the Labour party, replacing Anna Turley after a UK cabinet reshuffle [c24].

vocab.meaning: devices that block electronic radio signals
a change of positions within a government organization

stories.headline: Student protests over exam paper leaks trigger political fallout and parliamentary disruption in India
stories.body:
Massive student-led protests over national exam paper leaks have sparked political disruption and official investigations across India [c32, c35]. Indian Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned from his post following widespread demonstrations organized by students over the exam leaks [c35].

The protests in New Delhi led to violent clashes outside Parliament. Nearly 47 personnel from the Rapid Action Force were injured during student demonstrations outside Parliament, including six who suffered head injuries and four who suffered bone fractures [c33]. Following the events of July 20, the Central Reserve Police Force launched an inquiry to determine whether the Rapid Action Force was authorized to use pump-action pellet guns against the protesting students [c32].

Police response and surveillance methods have also become major points of dispute. Delhi Police alleged that 2,873 individuals present at protests in Jantar Mantar had criminal antecedents [c37]. Police stated that they identified 989 of these individuals by using a Facial Recognition System [c37]. In response to this tracking, student activist Aishe Ghosh filed a petition in the Delhi High Court seeking to declare mass facial recognition surveillance of protesters unconstitutional [c34]. Meanwhile, political groups have entered discussions; the Cockroach Janta Party demanded the withdrawal of all criminal cases filed against demonstrators as part of a negotiated settlement with the Indian government [c38].

The fallout from the police response has caused severe disruption in the Indian parliament. The Rajya Sabha was adjourned for a sixth consecutive day after opposition members demanded that Home Minister Amit Shah apologize for police action against protesting students [c36].

In a separate national security update, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah commended the Central Reserve Police Force on its Raising Day [c31]. They praised the force for eliminating Left-wing extremism within a set deadline of March 31, 2026 [c31].

vocab.meaning: past records or events, especially criminal history
temporarily stopped an official meeting or session

stories.headline: India summons Ukrainian ambassador and Russian diplomat following attacks on merchant ships
stories.body:
India has taken diplomatic action after multiple Indian seafarers were killed in maritime attacks connected to the Russia-Ukraine war [c41, c44, c45]. India's Ministry of External Affairs summoned Ukrainian Ambassador Oleksandr Polishchuk to express serious concern over attacks targeting commercial shipping in the Black Sea [c41]. The move followed a July 19 attack on a cargo vessel departing Odesa port, which killed four Indian seafarers and critically injured another [c42]. India also summoned Russia's Chargé d'Affaires Vladimir Ladanov after four Indian sailors died on the MV Golden Leo on July 19 [c45].

In total, five Indian seafarers have been killed in the war, while two remain missing after an attack on the MV AGN Ragnar on July 25 [c44]. Earlier, on July 18, Indian Chief Officer Sagar Gupta was killed when drones hit the Marshall Islands-flagged MV Omorfi in Russian waters [c43]. In response, India's Ministry of External Affairs issued a formal advisory urging Indian citizens to assess security risks before accepting maritime work in the Black Sea [c46].

In related regional developments, drones from the Security Service of Ukraine struck an oil platform, a Russian missile boat, and sanctioned cargo vessels in the northern Caspian Sea [c40]. Meanwhile, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called Iranian retaliation threats "unjustified and groundless," labeling Tehran an accomplice to Russian aggression [c39].

vocab.meaning: officially ordered someone to come to an official meeting
people who work on ships at sea
